notes: Powersoft's own website (powersoft.com) is currently serving a temporary "site under renewal" placeholder for all product and datasheet URLs, including the canonical X4L datasheet PDF (powersoft_X4L_DS_EN_WEB.pdf) and the X Series User Guide — attempts to fetch them (including with a browser user-agent) returned the placeholder page, not the real document. sourceUrl above is the correct canonical Powersoft datasheet URL, but it was not retrievable live at research time; findings are instead corroborated via (1) Powersoft's own official X4 datasheet PDF (same document family, DO000170.01, successfully fetched and read in full — the X4L is the higher-power/3-phase-PSU sibling sharing the identical rear-panel connector layout and channel counts) and (2) multiple secondary sources (B&H, Full Compass, Bekafun, Kinovox, ManualsLib X4/X Series manuals, and search-indexed snippets of the actual Powersoft X4L datasheet/user guide) that consistently report: 4x XLR analog in, 2x XLR AES3 in (4 AES3 channels), 2x RJ45 Dante/etherCON (primary+secondary redundant), 2x Neutrik NL4MD speakON outputs (one per bridgeable channel pair), and a 5-pin Phoenix/Euroblock AC mains inlet (single/bi/three-phase 85-460VAC, no voltage selector). Ethernet grade (eth-1g) is inferred from "Gigabit Ethernet" support text, not an explicit port-label spec. Did not find any dedicated GPIO/logic/remote connector on the X4/X4L rear panel besides the AC-integrated remote-on/off sensing — could not fully confirm absence. AES3 outputs (as opposed to inputs) were not confirmed to exist as separate physical ports; the 2 AES3 XLR connectors appear to be inputs only (selectable/backup source), consistent across all sources. Power output figures (4x8200W@2ohm / 4x6800W@4ohm / 4x4800W@8ohm), 2U rack, 495mm depth, 24kg weight for the X4L were confirmed via search-indexed content matching the real Powersoft X4L spec sheet. Given the primary source could not be live-verified end-to-end, confidence is set to medium.
